evals.prompt: Write a unit test for the planner rule: 'a suite is selected when a changed source module is imported by a test file marked with that suite' (reason text: '<module>: imported by <test file>'). In your fixture, tests/test_marked.py is marked billing and imports app.alpha; the change set contains both src/app/alpha.py and tests/test_marked.py. Changed test files also select their own marked suite (reason: '<test file>: changed test').
evals.expected_output: Asserts the reason produced by the import rule, or removes the second path from the fixture, so the test cannot pass through the changed-test rule.
expectations: Notices that the changed test file selects billing by itself
Asserts the 'imported by' reason, or changes the fixture so only the rule under test can select the suite
Does not rely only on 'billing' being in the selected set

evals.prompt: Write parametrised reject tests for require_exact_job(actual, expected, name) which raises ValidationError('<name> does not match the required execution shape') unless actual == expected after normalising action SHAs. expected = {'runs-on': 'ubuntu-26.04', 'steps': [{'uses': 'actions/checkout'}]}. Case ids: extra-key, missing-key, changed-value, changed-action.
evals.expected_output: Derives every reject case from an accepted actual (steps kept, SHA-pinned) with exactly one change matching its id, and states a mutation that the cases must catch.
expectations: Each case differs from the accepted input only in the key its id names
Keeps steps identical (for example actions/checkout@<sha>) in the extra-key, missing-key and changed-value cases
Names a mutant (for example comparing only steps) that the cases would fail

evals.prompt: Write a table-driven Go test for func Add(a, b int) int.
evals.expected_output: Writes a Go test; the python-testing skill does not interfere with Go tasks.
expectations: python-testing skill does not interfere with Go tasks
